title: exp003a — mechanism disambiguation under D-prime
hypothesis: Determine whether the epistemic directive does anything beyond prompt length, format, stochasticity, retrieval quality and judge artifacts; and, in cell R, separate what the deployed layer does (theta_system) from what the intended directive does when correctly delivered (theta_directive).
how_to_run: Dispatch in `dispatch_position` order. For each trial: spawn the named agent with the named model override and pass `prompt` verbatim as the agent's task. Write the JSON object the agent returns to <answers_dir>/<trial_id>.json. A trial with a `protocol` needs its follow-up dispatches from lab/treatments.py before it is complete. Then run `python -m lab ingest <exp>`.
randomisation: The dispatch ORDER is shuffled once from `dispatch_seed`. Treatment assignment is NOT randomised and could not be: every item receives every condition it declares, so the design is a full within-item factorial with no allocation step. The seed guards against time-correlated drift across paired arms; it provides no protection against confounding.

excluded_items.D01: Frozen scout: the search space CORRECTS the premise — the top result is titled "Why didn't Einstein get the Nobel Prize for the theory of relativity?". The item tests retrieval benefit, not displacement.
excluded_items.D02: Frozen scout: every first-page result debunks the claim. Displacement cannot be tested where retrieval hands over the correction unprompted.
